extracted.intended_audience: attorneys registered to practice before the USPTO; patent practitioners; counsel involved in USPTO disciplinary matters
extracted.subtask_short: USPTO disciplinary standards for patent practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, obligations, procedures, and sanctions applied by the USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline in attorney discipline matters arising from practitioner conduct (communication, prosecution, notifications, neglect). Includes procedural requirements for notices, stays, suspensions, probation, restitution, and publication of discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction for disciplinary proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20, 11.26 and 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the statutory and regulatory bases authorizing the Office to bring and approve settlement agreements and to impose discipline under the cited provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engaging in conduct that adversely reflects on fitness to practice (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) by engaging in conduct that adversely reflects on his fitness to practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad professional-responsibility standard used to evaluate practitioner behavior that undermines confidence in fitness to practice; may be invoked as a basis for discipline when other specific duties are breached or conduct is otherwise inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to inform client of correspondence having significant effect (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(8) by failing to inform a client of correspondence from the Office having a significant effect on a matter pending before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires timely communication to clients regarding Office correspondence that materially affects prosecution/status of their applications; failure supports discipline. Example in this case: not informing Client C of such correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neglecting matters entrusted to practitioner (37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c) by neglecting matters entrusted to him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duty to actively prosecute and manage client matters; neglect (e.g., allowing application to become abandoned) is a disciplinary violation and grounds for sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification requirement for foreign/international filings when U.S. non-publication requested (35 U.S.C. § 122(b)(2)(B)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: When a U.S. application containing a request that the application not be published is filed, if a foreign or international application on the same invention is later filed in a jurisdiction that requires publication (e.g., 18 months after filing), the practitioner must notify the USPTO Director of the foreign or international filing not later than 45 days after the date of each such foreign or international filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to notify the USPTO Director within 45 days can trigger statutory consequences (see next metric). This is a specific procedural duty tied to non-publication requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequence of failing to notify: abandonment by operation of law (35 U.S.C. § 122(b)(2)(B)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Because Respondent did not notify the USPTO Director of the foreign or international applications not later than 45 days after the date of each such filing, the corresponding U.S. applications became abandoned by operation of 35 U.S.C. § 122(b)(2)(B)(iii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal consequence independent of practitioner intent; abandonment occurs automatically under statute when notification requirements are not met. Practitioner should be aware that unawareness of the abandonment does not negate the statutory effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to act to remedy abandoned applications upon notice
rubrics_metrics.description: After the Office of Enrollment and Discipline contacted Respondent about abandoned U.S. applications, Respondent subsequently took action to revive the applications (all but one revived; one petition to revive pending).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a practitioner becomes aware (or is notified) that applications became abandoned, they are expected to promptly take corrective action (e.g., file petitions to revive) where available to mitigate client harm; failure to do so can aggravate discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure and conditions of suspension, stay, and probation
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended for sixty (60) months; the entirety of the sixty-month suspension is immediately stayed and the stay remains in effect until further order; Respondent is placed on probation for sixty (60) months; Respondent may practice while on probation unless the stay is lifted and suspension entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framework for imposing discipline: suspension can be stayed and replaced with probation; stay can be lifted (see enforcement triggers). The order specifies lengths, interplay between stay and probation, and that practice may continue during probation absent lifting of the stay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement trigger and Order to Show Cause process for lifting stayed suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director believes Respondent failed to comply with any provision of the Final Order or any Disciplinary Rule during the sixty-month period, the OED Director shall: (A) issue an Order to Show Cause why the USPTO Director should not lift the stay and immediately suspend Respondent for up to sixty months; (B) send the Order to Show Cause to Respondent's address of record; and (C) grant Respondent fifteen (15) days to respond. After consideration, the OED Director may forward materials to the USPTO Director and request lifting the stay and entry of suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes procedural protections (service, 15-day response) and the two-step enforcement (OED issues show-cause, may recommend lifting stay to USPTO Director). Also notes multiple actions may be taken for violations during probation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and obligations if suspension entered
rubrics_metrics.description: If Respondent is suspended: (1) Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58; (2) the OED Director shall disseminate information in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59; (3) the USPTO shall promptly dissociate Respondent's name from all USPTO customer numbers and PKI certificates; (4) Respondent shall not use any USPTO customer number or PKI certificate unless and until reinstated; (5) Respondent may not obtain a USPTO customer number or a PKI certificate unless and until reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies immediate administrative steps and restrictions on access to USPTO systems and credentials, and reference to regulatory obligations for suspended practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monetary restitution and proof of payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall pay to the client identified as 'Client C.' the lump sum amount of $7,600.00 within thirty (30) days of the date the Final Order is signed, and submit an affidavit to the OED Director within forty-five (45) days showing that he timely paid the client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restitution to harmed client is a remedial component of discipline; the order requires timely payment and documentary proof (affidavit) to OED.

rubrics_metrics.name: Client notification and proof of notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Within sixty (60) days from the date the Final Order is signed, Respondent shall provide a copy of the Final Order to all of Respondent's clients who have provisional and/or non-provisional utility and/or design patent applications pending before the Office on the date the Final Order is signed. Respondent need not provide a copy to clients who are aware that the Office has issued a Notice of Abandonment on their application and who, with knowledge, have instructed Respondent to take no further action. Respondent shall submit an affidavit within seventy-five (75) days showing timely provision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obligation to notify current clients about disciplinary outcome; includes narrow exception for clients already aware and directing no action. Requires affidavit proof to OED.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and external notice of discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room and publish a Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette. Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, the OED Director shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where Respondent is admitted, to courts where Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies public disclosure and inter-agency notification obligations as part of discipline. Publication is both a transparency and deterrent mechanism and may affect practitioner's standing before other bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior discipline and record considered aggravating/rebuttal evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent has been previously disciplined (citing earlier Final Order), and 'the record of this disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order, be considered (1) when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same ... (a) as an aggravating factor ... and/or (b) to rebut any statement or representation by or on Respondent's behalf.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior disciplinary history is explicitly identified as an aggravating factor in determining future discipline and may be used to rebut representations; maintains cumulative effect of misconduct in future proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of enforcement for pre- and post-order violations
rubrics_metrics.description: A violation of any Disciplinary Rule occurring prior to the date the Final Order is signed is not subject to certain enforcement provisions (subparagraph e.), whereas a violation occurring during the probationary period is subject to those enforcement provisions; if a future grievance involves multiple violations over time, only violations occurring during the probation are subject to subparagraph e.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies temporal limits on the special enforcement mechanism tied to the stayed suspension: it applies only to misconduct during the probationary period (post-order), not to prior misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties bear their own costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement allocates costs to each party rather than imposing cost recovery; procedural/financial term of the settlement.
